redstone_help.heading: Redstone Block Description
redstone_help.redstone.summary: Carries redstone signals when placed on blocks.
redstone_help.redstone.detail1: Signal strength ranges from 0 to 15 and drops by 1 for each dust step.
redstone_help.redstone_torch.summary: Normally on; switches off when the block it is attached to is powered.
redstone_help.redstone_torch.detail2: Repeatedly switching off in a short time can burn it out temporarily.
redstone_help.redstone_block.summary: A constant power source that outputs strength 15.
redstone_help.redstone_block.detail1: Cannot be switched off by a signal, but can be moved by pistons.
redstone_help.repeater.summary: Sends a rear input forwards and restores its strength to 15.
redstone_help.repeater.detail1: Right-clicking sets a delay of 1–4 redstone ticks: 0.1–0.4 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.repeater.detail2: A powered repeater or comparator pointing into its side locks its current output state.
redstone_help.comparator.summary: Compares rear and side signal strengths, or reads how full a container is.
redstone_help.comparator.detail1: Compare mode: passes the rear signal if it is at least as strong as the strongest side input.
redstone_help.comparator.detail2: Subtract mode: outputs the rear input minus the strongest side input, with a minimum of 0.
redstone_help.comparator.detail3: Right-clicking changes modes. The small front torch is lit in subtract mode.
redstone_help.observer.summary: Detects block state changes at its face and sends a short pulse from its back.
redstone_help.observer.detail1: The red dot outputs strength 15 for 1 redstone tick.
redstone_help.observer.detail2: Detects changes such as crop growth and piston movement, but not every change to a block's internal data.
redstone_help.lever.summary: A manual switch that toggles on and off when right-clicked.
redstone_help.lever.detail1: Outputs strength 15 continuously while switched on.
redstone_help.lever.detail2: Does not turn off automatically. Its on or off state remains until toggled again.
redstone_help.stone_button.summary: Outputs a brief strength-15 signal when pressed.
redstone_help.stone_button.detail1: Turns off after 1 second at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.stone_button.detail2: Unlike wooden buttons, it cannot be pressed by arrows.
redstone_help.wood_button.summary: Outputs strength 15 when pressed by hand or hit by an arrow.
redstone_help.wood_button.detail1: A manual press lasts 1.5 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.wood_button.detail2: It stays powered while an arrow remains in contact with the button.
redstone_help.stone_pressure_plate.summa: Outputs strength 15 when a player or mob stands on it.
redstone_help.stone_pressure_plate.detai: Dropped items alone do not activate it.
redstone_help.wood_pressure_plate.summar: Detects players, mobs, dropped items and other entities resting on it.
redstone_help.wood_pressure_plate.detail: Outputs strength 15 regardless of the number of detected entities.
A single dropped item activates it.
redstone_help.light_weighted_pressure_pl: A gold pressure plate whose signal increases with the number of entities on it.
Adds 1 signal strength per entity, up to 15 at 15 or more entities.
A merged stack of dropped items counts as one entity, not as each individual item.
redstone_help.heavy_weighted_pressure_pl: An iron pressure plate for measuring larger numbers of entities.
1–10 entities give strength 1, 11–20 give 2, and 141 or more give the maximum 15.
A merged stack of dropped items counts as one entity.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.summary: Outputs a redstone signal based on sunlight.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.detail1: Signal strength changes with time, weather and sky light.
redstone_help.daylight_detector.detail2: Right-clicking switches between normal and inverted modes.
redstone_help.target.summary: Outputs a signal based on where a projectile hits it.
redstone_help.target.detail1: Hits closer to the center produce stronger signals, up to strength 15.
redstone_help.target.detail2: Adjacent redstone dust connects towards the target block.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.summary: Two facing hooks connected by string detect entities crossing the line.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.detail1: An attached tripwire outputs strength 15 when an entity touches the string.
redstone_help.tripwire_hook.detail2: Cutting connected string with shears does not trigger the hooks.
redstone_help.string.summary: Placed string forms tripwire that detects entities.
redstone_help.string.detail1: A continuous line of string connects two tripwire hooks facing each other.
redstone_help.string.detail2: Entities touching the connected string make the hooks output a redstone signal.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.summary: Detects nearby vibrations such as footsteps and block placement.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.detail1: Output strength depends on the distance to the vibration source.
redstone_help.sculk_sensor.detail2: A comparator reads the vibration frequency. Wool blocks vibration transmission.
redstone_help.calibrated_sculk_sensor.su: A side input selects the vibration frequency this sensor detects.
redstone_help.calibrated_sculk_sensor.de: An input of strength 1–15 at the amethyst face limits detection to that frequency.
Input 0 accepts all frequencies. It has a longer detection range than a regular sculk sensor.
redstone_help.piston.summary: Extends when powered to push blocks in front of it.
redstone_help.piston.detail1: Moves up to 12 blocks at once. Some blocks, such as obsidian, cannot be pushed.
redstone_help.piston.detail2: Only the arm returns when power is removed. It does not pull the front block back.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.summary: Pushes blocks and can pull the front block back when retracting.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.detail1: Moves up to 12 blocks, including blocks carried by attached slime or honey blocks.
redstone_help.sticky_piston.detail2: In Java Edition, a very short pulse can cause it to retract without pulling the front block back.
redstone_help.slime_block.summary: Carries attached neighboring blocks when moved by a piston.
redstone_help.slime_block.detail1: Attached blocks count towards the piston's 12-block movement limit.
redstone_help.slime_block.detail2: Does not stick to honey blocks.
redstone_help.honey_block.summary: A sticky block that carries neighboring blocks when moved by a piston.
redstone_help.honey_block.detail1: Does not stick to slime blocks. Attached blocks still count towards the movement limit.
redstone_help.honey_block.detail2: It does not conduct redstone power.
redstone_help.dispenser.summary: Uses or fires one stored item whenever it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.dispenser.detail1: Behavior depends on the item: shoots arrows, uses water buckets, applies bone meal and more.
redstone_help.dispenser.detail2: Constant power does not activate it repeatedly. It activates again when power turns off and then on.
redstone_help.dropper.summary: Sends one stored item forwards each time it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.dropper.detail1: Inserts into a container in front of it, or drops an item if there is no container.
redstone_help.dropper.detail2: Does not execute the functions of arrows or buckets. It activates again when power turns off and then on.
redstone_help.hopper.summary: Collects items from above and transfers them into the container its spout points toward.
redstone_help.hopper.detail1: Redstone power locks its own pulling and pushing of items.
redstone_help.hopper.detail2: Other hoppers can still insert into a locked hopper. A comparator can read its fullness.
redstone_help.crafter.summary: Crafts the arranged recipe when it receives a new redstone signal.
redstone_help.crafter.detail1: Clicking an empty slot toggles its enabled state. Disabled slots do not accept ingredients.
redstone_help.crafter.detail2: A comparator counts occupied or disabled slots, giving a signal from 0 to 9.
redstone_help.redstone_lamp.summary: A lamp that lights up when powered by redstone.
redstone_help.redstone_lamp.detail1: Emits light level 15 while on. Turns off after a short delay when power is removed.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.summary: Toggles between lit and unlit each time it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.detail1: It keeps its on/off state when power is removed and changes state at the next rising signal.
redstone_help.copper_bulb.detail2: A comparator reads strength 15 while it is lit. Oxidation reduces its light level.
redstone_help.note_block.summary: Plays its configured note when it receives a new power signal.
redstone_help.note_block.detail1: Right-clicking changes pitch. The block underneath changes the instrument.
redstone_help.note_block.detail2: Regular instruments require air directly above. A mob head on top plays that mob's sound instead.
redstone_help.tnt.summary: Redstone power primes it to explode after a short fuse.
redstone_help.tnt.detail1: An ordinary redstone activation gives a fuse of about 4 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.tnt.detail2: Removing power does not cancel primed TNT.
redstone_help.rail.detail1: Redstone can switch the direction of a curved rail at a junction.
redstone_help.rail.detail2: Regular rails have no mechanism to accelerate carts.
redstone_help.powered_rail.summary: Accelerates minecarts when powered and brakes them when unpowered.
redstone_help.powered_rail.detail1: A directly powered rail also activates connected powered rails.
redstone_help.powered_rail.detail2: Starting a stationary cart depends on track layout, such as a slope or a blocked end.
redstone_help.detector_rail.summary: Outputs strength 15 while a minecart is on it.
redstone_help.detector_rail.detail1: A comparator reads the fullness of a chest or hopper minecart on the rail.
redstone_help.activator_rail.summary: When powered, triggers special functions of passing minecarts.
redstone_help.activator_rail.detail1: Can eject passengers or prime TNT minecarts.
redstone_help.activator_rail.detail2: Also controls hopper minecart collection. Does not accelerate minecarts.
redstone_help.iron_door.summary: An iron door opened and closed by redstone power.
redstone_help.iron_door.detail2: Opens when powered and closes when power is removed.
redstone_help.iron_trapdoor.summary: An iron trapdoor opened and closed by redstone power.
redstone_help.iron_trapdoor.detail2: Opens when powered and closes when power is removed.
redstone_help.door.summary: A door you can open by hand or control with redstone.
redstone_help.door.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.trapdoor.summary: A trapdoor you can operate by hand or with redstone.
redstone_help.trapdoor.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.fence_gate.summary: A fence gate you can operate by hand or with redstone.
redstone_help.fence_gate.detail1: A change to powered opens it; a change to unpowered closes it.
redstone_help.fence_gate.detail2: Blocks passage like a fence when closed.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.summary: Outputs a redstone signal while players have it open.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail1: Signal strength equals the number of players viewing it, up to 15.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail2: A comparator reads stored-item fullness, rather than the number of viewers.
redstone_help.container.summary: A comparator can read how full this container is.
redstone_help.container.detail1: A comparator reads the container when its rear faces it. Empty gives 0; completely full gives 15.
redstone_help.container.detail2: The signal accounts for slot count and item stack limits, not just the total number of items.
redstone_help.lectern.detail1: A comparator reads the current page position as a strength from 1 to 15.
redstone_help.lectern.detail2: With no book, comparator output is 0.
redstone_help.composter.detail1: Empty gives 0, rising with each stage to 8 when ready to harvest.
redstone_help.composter.detail2: A hopper above can add compostable items; a hopper below can extract finished bone meal.
redstone_help.lightning_rod.summary: Briefly outputs strength 15 when struck by lightning.
redstone_help.lightning_rod.detail1: Requires an actual lightning strike. Rain alone does not activate it.
redstone_help.jukebox.summary: Outputs redstone while playing music; a comparator identifies the stored disc.
redstone_help.jukebox.detail1: Outputs strength 15 while a disc is playing.
redstone_help.jukebox.detail2: Comparator strength depends on the type of disc inside.
redstone_help.image.bulb_memory: Stays lit after power is removed
redstone_help.image.rail_empty: Detector rail · no cart · output off
redstone_help.image.rail_cart: Detector rail · cart detected · output on
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.1: Power travels through up to 8 connected powered rails in each direction from a directly powered rail.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.2: On a straight line with direct power supplied only to the center rail, 8 rails on each side plus the center gives 17 powered rails. The ninth rail on either side needs another power source.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.3: Distance counts connected rails, including slopes. A normal, detector or activator rail interrupts propagation through powered rails.
redstone_help.extra.powered_rail.4: An activated powered rail does not output power to neighboring redstone dust.
redstone_help.extra.activator_rail.1: Power propagates through up to 8 connected activator rails in each direction from a directly powered one.
redstone_help.extra.activator_rail.2: Powered rails and activator rails do not pass activation between the two types. Activator rails do not accelerate minecarts.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.1: Each right-click raises the pitch by one semitone, cycling through 25 pitches over two octaves. The actual register depends on the instrument.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.2: It plays once when power changes from off to on. Continuous power does not repeat the note.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.3: Block underneath → instrument (representative materials). A mob head above takes priority over the block below.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.4: Dirt, grass block and other default materials → harp / piano
redstone_help.extra.note_block.5: Stone, cobblestone and similar materials → bass drum
redstone_help.extra.note_block.6: Sand, gravel, concrete powder → snare drum
redstone_help.extra.note_block.7: Glass, sea lantern and similar materials → hi-hat / clicks
redstone_help.extra.note_block.8: Wood planks, logs and similar materials → bass
redstone_help.extra.note_block.24: Waxed copper blocks use the same sound as their matching oxidation stage. The copper entries above refer to full copper blocks.
redstone_help.extra.note_block.25: Heads placed on top: zombie, skeleton, wither skeleton, creeper, dragon and piglin. These sounds are not pitch-tuned. A player head can use a separately configured custom sound.
redstone_help.extra.repeater.1: Any input from 1 to 15 produces output 15. An input of 0 produces 0.
redstone_help.extra.repeater.2: Locking holds either the on or off state. The side locking signal must end before the repeater responds to its rear input again.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.1: Rear input 10 and side input 7 gives output 10 in compare mode and 3 in subtract mode.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.2: Rear input 7 and side input 10 gives 0 in both modes. When both sides have input, the stronger side is used.
redstone_help.extra.comparator.3: It can also read values such as container fullness, book pages or disc type. The meaning depends on the block behind it.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.1: It has 5 slots. It pulls from a container above and pushes into the container at its output.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.2: Ordinary container transfers move 1 item every 8 game ticks: 2.5 items per second at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.hopper.3: Picking up a dropped stack differs from transferring single items between containers. Multiple items from the stack can be collected together when space is available.
redstone_help.extra.piston.1: In Java Edition, pistons cannot move blocks with block entities, such as chests, barrels, furnaces or hoppers.
redstone_help.extra.piston.2: It cannot extend if an immovable block obstructs the push or if more than 12 blocks would need to move.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.1: It shares the normal piston's movement limits. In Java it cannot move block entities such as chests, barrels, furnaces or hoppers.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.2: On retraction it pulls the movable block immediately in front of the head. Blocks attached through slime or honey also count toward the movement limit.
redstone_help.extra.sticky_piston.3: A 1-redstone-tick pulse in Java can push a block out without pulling it back.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.1: Its vibration detection radius is 8 blocks. A vibration takes time to travel from its source to the sensor.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.2: It is active for 30 game ticks, followed by a 10-game-tick cooldown: 1.5 and 0.5 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.3: Its ordinary output strength depends on distance; its comparator frequency identifies the vibration type. These are different values.
redstone_help.extra.calibrated_sculk_sen: Its detection radius is 16 blocks, compared with 8 for a normal sculk sensor.
It is active for 10 game ticks and then cools down for 10 game ticks: 0.5 seconds each at the default tick rate.
The strength supplied to the amethyst input side selects a vibration frequency. It does not fix the output strength to that value.
redstone_help.extra.crafter.1: It uses a 3×3 crafting grid. Disabled slots count as empty for recipes and reject incoming ingredients.
redstone_help.extra.crafter.2: The result is ejected from the front or transferred into a container there when it can accept the item.
redstone_help.extra.copper_bulb.1: Light levels by oxidation stage: copper 15, exposed 12, weathered 8, oxidized 4.
redstone_help.extra.copper_bulb.2: A lit bulb gives comparator output 15 regardless of oxidation. Light level and redstone signal strength are different values.
redstone_help.extra.detector_rail.1: A minecart on the rail powers connected dust at strength 15. The signal turns off after the cart leaves.
redstone_help.extra.detector_rail.2: It detects ordinary minecarts too. Comparator output for a minecart's inventory is separate from its detection signal.
redstone_help.count.formula: Comparator output: 0 when empty; otherwise 1 + floor(14 × fullness).
redstone_help.table.brewing: Brewing stand · comparator output by contents
redstone_help.shelf.summary: Displays three item stacks. When powered, it swaps multiple hotbar slots at once.
redstone_help.shelf.detail1: Without power, interaction swaps the selected shelf slot with the item in the main hand.
redstone_help.shelf.detail2: Up to three powered shelves connect. Interacting swaps 3, 6 or 9 hotbar slots.
redstone_help.chiseled_bookshelf.summary: Holds six books. A comparator reads the last slot a book was inserted into or removed from.
redstone_help.big_dripleaf.summary: Tilts when stood on, but stays flat while powered by redstone.
redstone_help.big_dripleaf.detail1: Receiving power also restores a leaf that has already tilted.
redstone_help.big_dripleaf.detail2: A projectile hit can tilt it immediately. It is not a redstone power source.
redstone_help.wind_charge.summary: A projectile whose impact creates a wind burst that can interact with certain blocks.
redstone_help.wind_charge.detail1: It can press buttons, toggle levers and interact with doors, trapdoors, fence gates and bells.
redstone_help.wind_charge.detail2: A dispenser launches it; a dropper ejects it as an item.
redstone_help.beehive.detail1: The full honey level is 5. It can be harvested with an empty glass bottle or shears.
redstone_help.beehive.detail2: A dispenser containing glass bottles or shears can harvest it.
redstone_help.cake.detail1: A whole cake gives 14. Each bite reduces it by 2, leaving 2 for the final bite.
redstone_help.cake.detail2: Eating the last bite removes the block.
redstone_help.respawn_anchor.detail2: A dispenser can charge it using glowstone.
redstone_help.decorated_pot.summary: Stores one item stack. A comparator reads its fullness.
redstone_help.decorated_pot.detail1: An empty pot gives 0; a full stack gives 15.
redstone_help.decorated_pot.detail2: Hoppers and droppers can insert items, and hoppers can extract them.
redstone_help.bell.summary: Rings once when it receives a new redstone signal.
redstone_help.bell.detail1: Continuous power does not make it ring repeatedly.
redstone_help.bell.detail2: It can also be rung by hand, projectiles or a wind charge.
redstone_help.item_frame.summary: A comparator reads the displayed item's rotation as a signal from 1 to 8.
redstone_help.item_frame.detail1: An empty frame gives 0. Inserting and rotating an item changes the output.
redstone_help.item_frame.detail2: Read it with a comparator on the opposite side of the solid block supporting the frame.
redstone_help.copper_golem_statue.summar: Has four poses, read by a comparator as signal strengths 1–4.
redstone_help.copper_golem_statue.detail: Standing gives 1, sitting 2, running 3 and the star pose 4.
redstone_help.creaking_heart.summary: Its comparator output depends on the distance to its linked creaking.
redstone_help.creaking_heart.detail1: The closer the creaking, the stronger the signal. Without a linked creaking, the signal is 0.
redstone_help.creaking_heart.detail2: It must be between two correctly aligned pale oak logs to meet its activation conditions.
redstone_help.end_portal_frame.summary: A comparator can read whether an eye of ender is inserted.
redstone_help.end_portal_frame.detail1: It gives 0 without an eye and 15 with an eye.
redstone_help.end_portal_frame.detail2: Redstone power itself does not open the End portal.
redstone_help.command_block.summary: Executes configured commands. A comparator reads the previous execution's success count.
redstone_help.command_block.detail1: Impulse, chain and repeating blocks have different execution timing.
redstone_help.command_block.detail2: Whether redstone or a successful preceding command is required depends on its settings.
redstone_help.extra.shelf.1: Power changes the swapping mode; applying power alone does not move items. A player must interact.
redstone_help.extra.chiseled_bookshelf.1: Before any book interaction, output is 0. Removing the final book still leaves the last interacted slot's number.
redstone_help.extra.chiseled_bookshelf.2: Each slot holds one book, book and quill, written book or enchanted book.
redstone_help.extra.chiseled_bookshelf.3: Insertion by a hopper or dropper and extraction by a hopper also affect its comparator output.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.2: Java cauldrons do not store potions or dyed water.
redstone_help.extra.big_dripleaf.1: Without power, being stood on causes 10 game ticks of instability, then 10 ticks of partial tilt before full tilt.
redstone_help.extra.big_dripleaf.2: Full tilt normally resets after 100 game ticks, or 5 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.big_dripleaf.3: Redstone input prevents or resets tilt. An observer can detect its state changes.
redstone_help.extra.wind_charge.1: Wind does not open iron doors or iron trapdoors, or override door states held by redstone power.
redstone_help.extra.wind_charge.2: The wind charge does not emit a strength-15 wire signal itself. It changes the output by activating a button or lever.
redstone_help.extra.wind_charge.3: A dispenser launches it forward. Which blocks respond depends on the impact and surroundings.
redstone_help.extra.beehive.2: At honey level 5, a bottle collects a honey bottle and shears collect 3 honeycombs.
redstone_help.extra.beehive.3: Harvesting resets honey level and comparator output to 0.
redstone_help.extra.cake.2: A cake with a candle can also be read by a comparator.
redstone_help.extra.respawn_anchor.1: It holds up to 4 charges. Each glowstone adds one charge, including when dispensed.
redstone_help.extra.respawn_anchor.2: Using a charged anchor in a dimension that does not support it causes an explosion. Applying redstone power does not consume a charge.
redstone_help.extra.decorated_pot.1: It has one slot and cannot store multiple stacks of different item types.
redstone_help.extra.bell.1: A bell receives power but does not itself emit a redstone output signal.
redstone_help.extra.item_frame.1: An item's initial orientation gives 1. Each 45-degree rotation advances through 2–8, then back to 1.
The pose determines comparator strength, not oxidation or wax.
The statue block is distinct from a moving copper golem. These signals describe the placed statue.
redstone_help.extra.creaking_heart.1: Output decreases as the linked creaking moves away and reaches 0 at 32 blocks or more.
redstone_help.extra.creaking_heart.2: This is a distance signal, not container fullness. An unrelated creaking does not affect it.
redstone_help.extra.end_portal_frame.1: The signal only reports the inserted eye; it does not report whether the complete portal is active.
redstone_help.extra.command_block.1: Impulse runs once on a new signal, repeating runs while active, and chain follows the preceding execution chain.
redstone_help.extra.command_block.2: Editing and using commands follows the game's permissions. Comparator output reflects command success, not merely on/off power.
redstone_help.extra.lightning_rod.1: After a lightning strike it outputs 15 for 8 game ticks, or 0.4 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.extra.lightning_rod.2: Oxidation and wax do not change its redstone output behavior.
redstone_help.extra.lectern.1: The brief strength-15 page-turn pulse differs from the comparator's page-position output.
redstone_help.extra.composter.1: Composting levels run from 1 to 7; the finished bone-meal-ready level is 8.
redstone_help.extra.composter.2: Extracting bone meal at signal 8 empties it and returns the output to 0.
redstone_help.extra.target.1: Arrows and tridents hold the signal for 20 game ticks; other projectiles hold it for 8.
redstone_help.extra.target.2: Hit position determines signal strength, not projectile damage.
redstone_help.extra.dropper.1: It randomly selects a nonempty slot and outputs one item. Transfer can fail if the container in front cannot accept it.
redstone_help.extra.dropper.2: Water buckets, arrows and TNT remain items. It does not perform the dispenser's use, launch or ignition actions.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.1: Unlike a dropper, these items perform special actions when conditions allow. One nonempty slot is selected randomly.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.2: Arrows, snowballs, all three egg colors and experience bottles: launch as projectiles.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.3: Splash and lingering potions: throw potion projectiles.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.4: Firework rockets, fire charges and wind charges: launch their respective projectiles.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.5: Water, lava and powder-snow buckets: place their contents. Creature buckets also release the creature.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.6: Empty bucket: collect a water/lava source or powder snow in front. Flowing water or lava cannot be collected.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.7: Flint and steel: light a fire or ignite an applicable block in front, using durability.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.8: Bone meal: apply its growth effect to eligible crops or plants in front.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.9: Shears: shear an eligible entity or harvest honeycomb from a full bee nest/beehive.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.10: Glass bottle: collect water or harvest honey from a level-5 bee nest/beehive.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.11: Water bottle: turn an eligible dirt block in front into mud. It does not drink ordinary potions.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.12: Glowstone: charge a respawn anchor in front, up to four charges.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.13: Honeycomb: wax an eligible copper block in front.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.14: Brush: brush an armadillo in front to obtain a scute, using durability.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.15: TNT: dispense primed TNT rather than dropping the item.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.16: Boats/rafts are placed on water and minecarts on rails, including variants with attachments.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.17: Armor stand: place an armor-stand entity in front.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.18: Dispensable equipment such as armor, elytra and saddles: equip an eligible entity in front, subject to slot and equipment requirements.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.19: Chest: equip an eligible tamed donkey, mule or llama that can carry one.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.20: Carved pumpkin or wither skeleton skull: can complete the appropriate structure to create a golem or wither.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.21: Shulker box: place it as a block in front.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.22: Spawn egg: spawn the corresponding mob.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.23: A block that a sulfur cube can swallow can be fed to a sulfur cube in front. A sulfur cube bucket can also release its contents.
redstone_help.extra.dispenser.24: If conditions fail, the action may fail or the item may be ejected. A dispenser does not transfer ordinary items into a container in front like a dropper does.
redstone_help.image.statue_star: Copper golem statue · star pose · comparator 4
redstone_help.chest.summary: Stores items in 27 slots; joining two creates a 54-slot double chest.
redstone_help.chest.detail1: Two matching, side-by-side chests can join. Ordinary and trapped chests do not join each other.
redstone_help.chest.detail2: A solid block such as stone directly above it, or a cat sitting on it, prevents it from opening.
redstone_help.chest.detail3: Hoppers can insert and extract items. Breaking the chest block drops its contents.
redstone_help.barrel.summary: A 27-slot container that can be opened even with a block above it.
redstone_help.barrel.detail1: Adjacent barrels remain separate containers, each with 27 slots.
redstone_help.barrel.detail2: Can face up, down or sideways; a block in front of its opening does not prevent access.
redstone_help.barrel.detail3: Hoppers can insert and extract items. Breaking the barrel block drops its contents.
redstone_help.shulker_box.summary: A 27-slot box that retains its contents when broken and collected.
redstone_help.shulker_box.detail1: Place the collected shulker box again to access the items stored inside.
redstone_help.shulker_box.detail2: Its lid needs room to open. Color does not change its capacity or basic behavior.
redstone_help.shulker_box.detail3: A shulker box cannot contain another shulker box. Hoppers can insert and extract ordinary items.
redstone_help.copper_chest.summary: Stores items and supplies the items that a copper golem picks up for sorting.
redstone_help.copper_chest.detail1: A single copper chest has 27 slots; a double copper chest has 54.
redstone_help.copper_chest.detail2: A copper golem carries items from it to an ordinary or trapped chest that is empty or contains the same item type.
redstone_help.copper_chest.detail3: Oxidation and wax do not change its capacity. Hoppers can also insert and extract items.
redstone_help.furnace.summary: Uses fuel to process ores, food and other materials with smelting recipes.
redstone_help.furnace.detail1: Has one input, fuel and output slot. Processing requires a valid input and fuel.
redstone_help.furnace.detail2: A typical default smelting recipe takes 200 game ticks per item, or 10 seconds at the default tick rate.
redstone_help.furnace.detail3: Hoppers can insert ingredients from above, fuel from the sides and extract results from below.
redstone_help.blast_furnace.summary: Smelts ores and eligible metal equipment faster than a furnace.
redstone_help.blast_furnace.detail1: Only blasting recipes work; ordinary food-cooking and sand-smelting recipes do not.
redstone_help.blast_furnace.detail2: Default blasting takes 100 game ticks, or 5 seconds at the default tick rate—half the furnace time for the same material.
redstone_help.blast_furnace.detail3: Uses three slots for input, fuel and output, with the same hopper directions as a furnace.
redstone_help.smoker.summary: Cooks eligible food faster than a furnace.
redstone_help.smoker.detail1: Only smoking recipes work; ores and sand cannot be processed.
redstone_help.smoker.detail2: Default smoking takes 100 game ticks, or 5 seconds at the default tick rate—half the furnace time for the same food.
redstone_help.smoker.detail3: Uses three slots for input, fuel and output, with the same hopper directions as a furnace.
redstone_help.brewing_stand.summary: Uses blaze powder as fuel to brew up to three potion bottles at once.
redstone_help.brewing_stand.detail1: Has three bottle slots, one ingredient slot and one fuel slot. One ingredient processes the eligible bottles together.
redstone_help.brewing_stand.detail2: A brewing operation takes 400 game ticks, or 20 seconds at the default tick rate. One blaze powder provides fuel for 20 operations.
redstone_help.brewing_stand.detail3: Brewing requires a valid ingredient, bottles and available fuel; redstone power does not directly start or stop it.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail3: Has 27 storage slots; joining two trapped chests creates 54 slots.
redstone_help.trapped_chest.detail4: Does not join ordinary chests. A solid block above it or a sitting cat prevents opening.
redstone_help.cauldron.summary: Holds water, lava or powder snow, with contents transferred using buckets or bottles.
redstone_help.cauldron.detail1: Water and powder snow have three fill levels; lava is either absent or full.
redstone_help.cauldron.detail2: Use an empty bucket to collect full contents. Glass bottles remove one water level, and water bottles add one.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.1: An empty cauldron gives 0; water and powder snow give 1–3 by fill level; lava gives 3.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.3: Collects drips below a pointed-dripstone stalactite supplied with water or lava above. One lava drip fills it completely.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.4: During actual snowfall, an exposed empty or powder-snow cauldron gradually collects powder snow. A cold location alone does not fill it.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.5: During rain, an exposed empty or water cauldron gradually fills with water. A roof blocks both rain and snow.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.6: Weather does not replace the contents with another material. Snowfall does not turn water in a cauldron into powder snow.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.7: Water can remove dye from eligible equipment or a shulker box, or remove a banner's last pattern. Each wash uses one water level.
redstone_help.extra.cauldron.8: Different contents can produce the same strength, so a comparator signal alone does not identify the material.
redstone_help.table.double: Double chest, %s slots · count → comparator output
redstone_help.count.assumptions: Fullness is the average fill fraction of all slots, including empty ones. If items with different maximum stack sizes are mixed, their total count alone is insufficient.
redstone_help.count.stack_sizes: The 64/slot, 16/slot and 1/slot headings mean the maximum number of that item type that can stack in one slot.
redstone_help.count.stack_examples: Examples: stone stacks to 64, ender pearls to 16, and swords to 1. A single non-stackable item therefore fills its slot completely.
redstone_help.count.ranges: Choose the column for your item, find its total individual-item count in the container, then read the output on the right. Values count items, not stacks. Each column assumes only items with that stack limit; — means an unreachable output.
redstone_help.count.brewing: The table gives comparator output for individual water bottles, ingredients and blaze powder stored in the brewing stand. Bottles stack to 1; the example ingredients and powder stack to 64. The internal fuel meter is excluded.
redstone_help.extra.jukebox.1: After playback ends, comparator output remains while the disc stays inside. Removing the disc returns it to 0.
redstone_help.extra.jukebox.2: Some discs share the same comparator output. The output alone cannot uniquely identify every disc.
redstone_help.extra.jukebox.3: Hoppers can insert and extract discs. During playback, the jukebox powers and locks a hopper directly below it.
redstone_help.extra.jukebox.4: The table lists all 22 default Java 26.2 discs. These are comparator readings, distinct from the jukebox's own strength-15 output during playback.
redstone_help.amethyst_block.summary: When touching a sculk sensor, re-emits a detected vibration at the same frequency.
redstone_help.amethyst_block.detail1: Must directly touch a face of a normal or calibrated sculk sensor, including above or below. Diagonal or separated blocks do not resonate.
redstone_help.amethyst_block.detail2: When the sensor activates, a new vibration originates at the amethyst block. Other sensors can detect it; their output strength depends on the new travel distance.
redstone_help.amethyst_block.detail3: Resonance uses a regular block of amethyst. Budding amethyst, amethyst buds and clusters are not vibration resonators.
redstone_help.wool.summary: Blocks vibration paths between an event and a sculk sensor.
redstone_help.wool.detail1: Wool must lie in the vibration's path to block it. Placing wool beside a sensor does not block every direction.
redstone_help.wool.detail2: Walking on wool, or placing or breaking wool, does not trigger a sculk sensor. All 16 colors behave alike.
redstone_help.wool.detail3: Wool carpets also suppress footsteps on them, but do not block vibrations passing from elsewhere as wool blocks do.
redstone_help.wool_carpet.summary: A thin floor covering that suppresses sculk-detectable footsteps when walked on.
redstone_help.wool_carpet.detail1: Placing or breaking wool carpet is also excluded from vibration detection. All wool carpet colors behave alike.
redstone_help.wool_carpet.detail2: Unlike wool blocks, carpets do not occlude vibration paths. Vibrations originating beyond a carpet can still reach a sensor.
redstone_help.image.amethyst_resonating: Amethyst resonance · receiving sensor lights lamp
redstone_help.image.wool_blocked: White wool blocks the path · no detection
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.4: Wool blocks occlude vibration paths. Wool carpets suppress footsteps on them but do not block passing vibrations.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.5: A block of amethyst touching a face re-emits the detected frequency. Another sensor's output strength depends on the new travel distance.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.6: Waterlogging preserves vibration detection and redstone output. It silences the sensor's own activation sound rather than disabling detection.
redstone_help.extra.sculk_sensor.7: The table gives representative events for frequencies 1–15. A comparator reads this frequency while the sensor is active. A calibrated sensor's input 1–15 accepts only that frequency; 0 disables filtering.
redstone_help.extra.calibrated_sculk_sen: Wool blocks occlude vibration paths. Wool carpets suppress footsteps on them but do not block passing vibrations.
A block of amethyst touching a face re-emits the detected frequency. Another sensor's output strength depends on the new travel distance.

redstone_help.chiseled_bookshelf.detail1: A comparator reads the last used slot: 1, 2, 3 across the top row and 4, 5, 6 across the bottom, left to right.
redstone_help.chiseled_bookshelf.detail2: The comparator reading does not represent book count or inventory fullness.
redstone_help.extra.beehive.1: A comparator reads honey level 0–5 from either bee nests or beehives, not the number of bees inside.
redstone_help.extra.decorated_pot.2: One non-stackable item fills the slot completely, so a comparator reads strength 15.
redstone_help.extra.item_frame.2: A comparator reads rotation the same way for glow item frames. The signal is unrelated to item count.
redstone_help.respawn_anchor.detail1: Charge levels 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 give comparator outputs 0, 3, 7, 11 and 15.
redstone_help.lectern.summary: Holds an open book and emits a short redstone pulse when a page is turned.
redstone_help.composter.summary: Converts compostable material into bone meal. A comparator reads its composting level.
redstone_help.beehive.summary: Houses bees and stores honey. A comparator reads the honey level as a signal from 0 to 5.
redstone_help.cake.summary: A food block eaten one slice at a time. A comparator reads the remaining cake, decreasing as it is eaten.
redstone_help.respawn_anchor.summary: Sets a respawn point in the Nether and is charged with glowstone. A comparator reads the remaining charges.
redstone_help.extra.lectern.2: For a book with at least two pages, the first page gives 1 and the last gives 15. A one-page book gives 15.
redstone_help.extra.shelf.3: One or two connected shelves swap the rightmost 3 or 6 hotbar slots; three swap all 9.
redstone_help.extra.shelf.2: Viewed from the front, occupied left, middle and right slots contribute 1, 2 and 4. A comparator connected behind the shelf reads their sum from 0 to 7; the count within each stack does not matter.

modmenu.descriptionTranslation.redstone_:
A client-side guide to redstone block functions and operating conditions, shown directly in inventory tooltips.

Hold Shift to open photos and detailed information, then scroll with the mouse wheel.
Press the pin key (default H) while viewing Shift details to keep the guide open. Click its contents, pause photos or step backward/forward. Close with Esc.
Change the pin key in Options → Controls → Key Binds → Redstone Block Description.

/rbd on: enable · /rbd off: disable
/rbd toggle: switch · /rbd status: check
Your on/off preference is saved between sessions.

Includes 233 vanilla items, 71 topics and 190 real in-game photos. Reference tables cover container quantities and comparator output, music discs, note-block instruments and dispenser actions.

Korean and English. Requires Minecraft Java 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.5+, Fabric API 0.160.0+26.2 and Java 25+. No server installation needed.
